name: GO Classes Test Series 2023 | NIELIT Mock Test 7

question.text:
Based on the given statements and conclusions and mark the correct answer.

Statement $1:$ All apples are red.
Statement $2: $ Some red things are fruits.

Conclusion I: Some fruits are apples.
Conclusion II: All red things are fruits.

  1. Neither I nor II follow
  2. Only conclusion II follow
  3. Only conclusion I follow
  4. Either I or II follow

A man walks $5$ metres straight and then $10$ meters to the right. After this he continuously turns left and every time walks $10,5$ and $10$ meters respectively. How far is he now from his starting point?

  1. $5 \sqrt{3}$ metres
  2. $3 \sqrt{5}$ metres
  3. $5 \sqrt{2}$ metres
  4. 10 metres

The HCF and LCM of the two numbers are $12$ and $924$ respectively. Then the number of such pairs is ____________.

  1. $0$
  2. $1$
  3. $2$
  4. $3$

The average age of $8$ men is increased by $2$ years, when two of them, whose ages are $20$ years and $24$ years respectively, are replaced by two women. What is the average age of these women?

  1. $36$ years
  2. $30$ years
  3. $40$ years
  4. $42$ years

person was asked to state his age in years. reply was, Take my age three years hence, multiply it by $3$ and then subtract three times my age three years ago and you will know how old I am. What was the age of the person (years)?

  1. $18$
  2. $20$
  3. $24$
  4. $32$

Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to that expressed in the main pair.

$\text{EVERGREEN : TREE : :}$

  1. reservoir: sea
  2. carnivore : prey
  3. cumulus : cloud

  4. $\dfrac{100 \sqrt{2}}{\pi} \mathrm{cm}$

  1. $156$
  2. $312$
  3. $78$

The table shows the percentage of literate people in $6$ cities.

This table also shows the ratio of males to females among literate people.

  1. $5000$
  2. $10000$
  3. $15000$
  4. $20000$

A student took five papers in an examination, where the full marks were the same for each paper. His marks in these papers were in the proportion of $6: 7: 8: 9 : 10.$ In all papers together, the candidate obtained $60 \%$ of the total marks. Then the number of papers in which he got more than $50 \%$ marks is __________.

  1. $2$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. $5$

$\text{‘X}+\text{Y’}$ means $\text{‘X}$ is the father of $\text{Y’}  , \text{‘X}-\text{Y’}$ means $\text{‘X}$ is the wife of $\text{Y’}  , \text{‘X} \times \text{Y’}$ means $\text{‘X}$ is the brother of $\text{Y’}  , \text{‘X} \div \text{Y’}$ means, $\text{‘X}$ is the mother of $\text{Y’}$ and $\text{‘X}=\text{Y’}$ means $\text{‘X}$ is the sister of $\text{Y’}$ . On the basis of this information, what does $\text{X}+\text{Y}-\text{Z}$ mean?

  1. $\text{X}$ is the father-in-law of $\text{Z}$
  2. $\text{Z}$ is the father of $\text{X}$
  3. $\text{Z}$ is the niece of $\text{X}$
  4. $\text{X}$ is the brother of $\text{Z}$

  1. $22$
  2. $21$

If the expressions $\text{‘E}<\text{J} \leq \text{H}>\text{Z’}, \text{‘H} \leq \text{Y’}$ and $\text{‘E}>\text{F’}$ are true, which of the following conclusions will be definitely false?

  1. $\text{F}<\text{Y}$
  2. $\text{Y}>\text{E}$
  3. $\text{F}<\text{H}$
  4. All are true

Two pipes $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ can fill a cistern in $12$ minutes and $15$ minutes respectively but a third pipe $\text{C}$ can empty the full tank in $6$ minutes, $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are kept open for $5$ minutes in the beginning and then $\text{C}$ is also opened. In what time is the cistern emptied?

  1. $30 \mathrm{~min}$.
  2. $33 \mathrm{~min}$.
  3. $37 \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~min}$.
  4. $45 \mathrm{~min}$.

To have more fun, they indulge only in one activity per day, i.e. either they went for yoga or played tennis each day. There were days when they were lazy and stayed home all day long. There were $24$ mornings when they did nothing, $14$ evenings when they stayed at home, and a total of $22$ days when they did yoga or played tennis. For how many days Shyam stayed with Ram?

Match the following:
$$
\begin{array}{cl|cl}
\hline (\text{P}) & \text{Lexical analysis} & \text{(i)} & \text{Leftmost derivation} \\
\hline (\text{Q}) & \text{Top down parsing} & \text{(ii)} & \text{Type checking} \\

Consider a modification to QUICKSORT such that each time PARTITION is called, the median of the partitioned array is found (in $\Theta(n)$ time) and used as pivot. What is the running time of this algorithm:

  1. $\Theta(n)$
  2. $\Theta(n^2)$
  3. $\Theta(n \log n)$
  4. $\Theta(n^3)$

Given the function $F(A, B, C, D) = \sum(0, 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 10, 14)$, determine the simplified expression for $F$
  1. $B'D'+A'C'D'+A'B'C'+A'BCD$
  2. $B'D'+A'C'D'+A'BC'+A'BCD$
  3. $B'D+A'C'D'+A'B'C'+A'BCD$
  4. $B'D'+A'CD'+A'B'C'+A'BCD$

  1. $(a + bc + b'c')(abc')'$

What will be the output of the following Java program when executed?

public class Question {
    public static void main(String args[]) {
        int product = 1;
        int N = Integer.parseInt(args[0]);
        for(int i = 1; i <= N; i++)
            product *= i;
        System.out.println(product);
    }
}
  1. Print the value of $\mathrm{N}!$
  2. Print the value of $\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{N}+1) / 2$
  3. Print the value of $1 \times 3 \times 5 \times \ldots \times \mathrm{N}$
  4. Print the value of $1 ! \times 2 ! \times 3 ! \times \ldots \times \mathrm{N}$ !

If we need to guarantee that the running time will be no worse than n log n, which sorting methods could we use?

  2. quicksort

In a system with $\text{N}$ bytes of physical RAM and $\text{M}$ bytes of virtual address space per process, where pages and frames are $\text{K}$ bytes in size, and each page table entry is $\text{P}$ bytes in size, what is the size of the page table for a process?

What is the probability that Shyam does not have COVID disease ?

  1. $1.014\%$
  2. $2.041\%$
  3. $3.041\%$

  1. Memory footprint

Suppose a method $\text{M}_1$ calls a method $\text{M}_2$, which in turn, calls another method $\text{M}_3$. The level of testing that tests for the interface of calls from $\text{M}_1$ to $\text{M}_2$ and then to $\text{M}_3$ is called as ________.

  1. Functional testing.
  2. Unit testing.
  3. Integration testing.
  4. System testing.

Suppose you are given an implementation of a queue of integers the operations that can be performed on the queue is

  1. empty $(Q)$ - returns true if the queue empty, false characters
  2. delete $(Q)$ - deletes the element at the front of the queue and return its value.
  3. insert $(Q, i)$ - insert the integer $i$ at the rear of queue.

Consider the following function

void f(queue Q)
{
    int i;
    if (! isempty(Q))
        {   
            i = delete(Q);
            f(Q);
            insert(Q, i);
    }
}


What operation is performed by the above function $f?$ 

  1. Leaves the queue $Q$ unchanged
  2. Reverse the order of element in the queue
  3. Deletes the element at the front of the queue $Q$ and inserts
    it at the rear keeping the other elements in the same order
  4. Empties the queue $(Q)$

Consider the grammar given below:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{PQ} \mid \mathrm{P} \\
& \mathrm{Q} \rightarrow \mathrm{aPQ} \mid \mathrm{aP} \\
& \mathrm{P} \rightarrow \mathrm{a}
\end{aligned}
$$
Which of the following is an equivalent operator precedence grammar for the above CFG?

  1. $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{S} & \rightarrow \mathrm{aQ} \mid \mathrm{P} \\ \mathrm{Q} & \rightarrow \mathrm{aQ} \mid \mathrm{a} \\ \mathrm{P} & \rightarrow \mathrm{a}\end{aligned}$
  2. $\begin{aligned}
    & \mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{P}|\mathrm{PaP}| \mathrm{PaS}\\
    & \mathrm{P} \rightarrow \mathrm{a}
    \end{aligned}$
  3. Both of them
  4. None of them

  1. The member can be directly accessed in member functions belonging to that class
